panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A is a radiograph of the lower extremities (femur/tibia) in an infant with opsismodysplasia. It explicitly shows delayed/absent ossification centers, a characteristic finding of the disease. B: Panel B is a radiograph of the upper extremity showing shortened long bones, consistent with skeletal dysplasia (Opsimosysplasia). C: Panel C is a radiograph of the feet showing irregular ossification and metaphyseal cupping, consistent with opsismodysplasia. D: Panel D is a radiograph of the spine showing platyspondyly, which is mentioned in the context of this case of opsismodysplasia.

panels.figure_caption: Case 2, Initial skeletal survey at 9 days of life (A) [10/09/08] demonstrates lack of visualization of the distal femoral and proximal tibial ossification centers, (B) relatively short long bones of the left upper extremity and (C) feet with metaphyseal cupping and irregular ossification of the talus and calcaneus. The degree of platyspondyly (D) is less than that of her sibling on lateral spine radiographs.
in_text_mentions: brother’s skeletal dysplasia, she was evaluated for the diagnosis of opsismodysplasia. Radiographically, no secondary ossification centers were identified, specifically to include the proximal tibial and distal femoral epiphyses, which should be present at this age. (Figure 4) The metacarpals and phalanges of her hands and feet were shortened with metaphyseal cupping. Platyspondyly was present and the symphysis pubis was poorly ossified. Her talus and calcaneus were ossified, but irregular in shape. Her ribs were mildly shortened with cupped anterior rib ends. Her serum phosphorous was normal.
